run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T04:56:19Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Alert RequestErrorRate on otel-demo/frontend-proxy reflects real error responses recorded by the proxy: its ingress (server) and 'router frontend egress' (client) spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and its access log shows 500s on POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout from 04:58:53Z to 04:59:21Z plus sporadic 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on GET /api/products/*. The largest excursion (1.65% of ingress spans erroring over 04:57:32-05:07:32 vs 0.016% over the preceding 10 minutes) coincides with a rollout restart of the cart Deployment at 04:58:49Z: the single old cart pod was deleted at 04:58:52Z, three seconds after the new cart container started, and during that bucket the frontend's gRPC client calls to cart stayed at normal volume while cart's own server spans collapsed to ~10% of normal, i.e. the requests were not reaching cart. The cart container has no readiness/startup probe, so the Service routed traffic to the replacement pod before it was serving. That explains the 500 burst and the frontend's own error spans on cart-dependent routes. Two things remain unresolved: the alert is reported as firing since 04:56:19Z, ~2.5 min before the first 5xx log line I could see, and the alert rule expression is not readable from this Prometheus, so the exact trigger/evaluation window is unknown; and a low rate of ingress-only 503 errors continues after the burst (4.28 ingress errors in 05:06-05:16 with zero frontend-proxy egress and zero frontend error spans), which on a '>0' threshold can keep the alert firing. A flagd fault-injection setting cartFailure=on exists but does not match the observed path and is kept as a hypothesis, not the cause.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span error ratio: ingress was near zero through 04:57 (0.000303 at 04:57:19), rose to 0.0285 at 05:01:19 and 0.0289 at 05:03:19, and fell back to 0.0015-0.0022 by 05:11-05:13; 'router frontend egress' was zero at every point except 0.0273 at 05:01:19 and 0.0277 at 05:03:19.

On 10-minute windows the frontend-proxy ingress error ratio was 0.00167 (04:37:32-04:47:32), 0.000162 (04:47:32-04:57:32), 0.0165 (04:57:32-05:07:32) and 0.00216 (05:07:32-05:17:32); the series only has samples from about 04:39 onward.

frontend-proxy access logs show a burst of 500 responses with upstream 'frontend' and flag via_upstream on POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout running from 04:58:53Z to 04:59:21Z (about 95 lines), and separate single 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' entries on GET /api/products/* at 04:57:06Z, 05:00:06Z, 05:00:07Z, 05:01:12Z, 05:03:25Z and 05:05:54Z.

The frontend service's own error spans are confined to one 2-minute bucket ending 05:01:00Z: grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 69.3, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 30.7, tcp.connect 9.3, POST /api/cart 69.3, GET /api/cart 30.7, POST /api/checkout 24, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 24 and 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 100; every other 2-minute bucket from 04:52 to 05:12 is zero.

In the 2-minute bucket ending 05:01:00Z the frontend client spans for cart remained at normal volume (grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 128, GetCart 114.7) while cart's own server spans collapsed (POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 13.3 vs 114-242 elsewhere in 04:52-05:12; POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 30.7 vs 197-430).

Kubernetes events in otel-demo show the cart Deployment rolling at 04:58:49-04:58:52Z: ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d created pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz (Scheduled 04:58:49Z, cart container Started 04:58:51Z), Deployment cart scaled that ReplicaSet 0->1, ReplicaSet cart-755465879b reported 'Deleted pod: cart-755465879b-rh5r4' and kubelet reported 'Stopping container cart' on cart-755465879b-rh5r4 at 04:58:52Z, with Deployment cart scaled the old ReplicaSet 1->0.

The replacement cart ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d differs from cart-755465879b only by pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T04:58:49Z: same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, same env, same init container busybox:latest wait-for-valkey-cart, and the cart container declares readinessProbe null in both templates.
Deployment cart in otel-demo has replicas 1, RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25%, and its cart container has readinessProbe, livenessProbe and startupProbe all null.

The only cart series with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR returned for 05:01-05:16Z was span_name flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, with value 0 at every point; no cart server-span ERROR series was returned.

Cart server spans continued to be recorded for cart's operations through the window (e.g. HGET, HMSET, EXPIRE, POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart) - with STATUS_CODE_UNSET only.

Pod status: cart-84889c965d-tkxdz is Running and ready with 0 restarts and startTime 2026-11-17T04:58:49Z; frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt are Running/ready with 0 restarts and lastState.terminated null; fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh is Running/ready with restartCount 1 and lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh recorded a second 'Created container: fraud-detection' and 'Started container fraud-detection' at 05:04:20Z (count 2 for each event), consistent with the OOMKilled restart; no error spans for fraud-detection appear in the sampled topk lists.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo currently defines flag cartFailure with defaultVariant 'on', state ENABLED, description 'Fail cart service'; the flagd Deployment's current ReplicaSet flagd-77f6d5b95d carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T04:29:34Z.

Cart pod logs sampled from 05:08:52Z to 05:09:27Z show ordinary request handling lines ('AddItemAsync called with userId=...', 'GetCartAsync called with userId=...', 'EmptyCartAsync called with userId=...') with no error text in the returned lines.

In the last 10 minutes of the window (05:06-05:16Z) frontend-proxy ingress still recorded 4.28 error spans while 'router frontend egress' recorded 0 and every frontend operation recorded 0, so the residual errors are ingress-only and not produced by frontend spans.

The topk error-span queries for 04:56-05:02Z and 05:06-05:16Z returned frontend-proxy and frontend operations as the only high entries; the only other nonzero entry was recommendation span /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at 1.2 per 6m at 05:02Z.

The 500 burst 04:58:53-04:59:21Z was caused by the cart Deployment rolling its only pod: the new cart container started at 04:58:51Z, the old pod was stopped at 04:58:52Z, and because the cart container has no readiness/startup probe the Service sent frontend traffic to the replacement pod before its gRPC endpoint was accepting connections (frontend-side tcp.connect error spans and cart server-span collapse support this).

Continued firing of an alert whose stated condition is error rate above 0 can be sustained by the sporadic ingress-only 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' entries on GET /api/products/* (one to four per 10 minutes, still visible at 05:05:54Z, with 4.28 ingress error spans in 05:06-05:16Z); the reason those frontend upstream connections reset is not established.

flagd flag cartFailure='on' is a fault-injection setting that can fail the cart service, but it does not match the observed failure path here: cart server spans collapsed (requests never arrived) rather than showing cart-side errors, cart produced no ERROR spans in 05:01-05:16Z, and the sampled cart logs show normal handling; when the flag was changed cannot be verified.

frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt and frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 were Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no terminated previous container, so the frontend-proxy errors are not explained by a crash or restart of those pods.

A frontend-proxy pod crash/restart as the cause of its error responses is rejected: the pod stayed Running/ready with 0 restarts across the window and the log reader found no previous container instance.

Add a readinessProbe (and startupProbe) to the cart container, and set maxUnavailable: 0 plus minReadySeconds on the cart Deployment, so a rollout does not stop the old pod until the replacement is actually serving on port 8080.

Investigate the recurring frontend upstream connection resets that frontend-proxy logs as 503 UC on GET /api/products/*, since they keep frontend-proxy error rate above the alert's reported above-0 condition after the cart burst ended.

Confirm why Deployment cart (restartedAt 04:58:49Z) and Deployment flagd (restartedAt 04:29:34Z) were rolled and whether flagd flag cartFailure='on' is intended, before treating either as deliberate fault injection.

Review the fraud-detection container memory limit: fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh restarted once with lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled and a fresh container start at 05:04:20Z; this is a separate signal not tied to the frontend-proxy errors.

gaps: The alert rule itself could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with match {severity="warning"}, type=alert, both returned no rules (status no_data), so the alert's exact expression, threshold and reported current value 0.0111 are unverified; the alert's stated start 04:56:19Z is ~2.5 minutes before the first 5xx line visible in frontend-proxy logs (04:57:06Z), so the initial trigger is unresolved.
change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what issued the kubectl rollout restart annotations on Deployment cart (04:58:49Z) and Deployment flagd (04:29:34Z) is unknown.

Logs of the removed cart pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 and previous-container logs for cart, frontend and frontend-proxy are unavailable, so cart-side or frontend-side error text before/at 04:58:5xZ could not be checked.
The frontend container's stdout returned no lines for 04:50-05:06Z (unfiltered query), so frontend exception messages were not verifiable; only its span statuses were.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend-proxy (04:54-05:06Z) or error-tagged frontend spans (04:50-05:05Z) even though traces_list_services lists both services, so span error details and parent-child edges remain unknown.
trace span metrics have samples only from about 04:39Z in this window, so no long pre-incident baseline exists and the onset of the sporadic 503 UC errors before 04:54Z could not be established.

Cart server span counts are bucketed in a way that does not align exactly with the 04:58:53-04:59:21Z log burst (the 05:01:00Z 2-minute bucket shows a full collapse), so the exact duration of cart unavailability derived from spanmetrics is uncertain.
The state and change time of the flagd cartFailure flag during the incident cannot be verified from a point-in-time ConfigMap read.
next_steps: Obtain the RequestErrorRate rule definition (query, for-duration, threshold and evaluation window) from the Prometheus/Alertmanager that produced the alert, to confirm whether it fired on the cart-restart burst or on the sporadic ingress 503s.
Add readiness/startup probes to the cart container and set maxUnavailable: 0 / minReadySeconds on Deployment cart, then verify a rollout causes no frontend 500s.
Capture and inspect frontend application logs (and enable log output if it is suppressed) around a cart rollout to confirm the cart-unreachable error text.
Trace the origin of 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started on GET /api/products/* (frontend upstream resets) as a separate follow-up, since it keeps frontend-proxy error rate nonzero.
Check the fraud-detection container's memory limit and usage history given its OOMKilled restart at 05:04:20Z.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
